What It Covers

Coverage Sized for the Costs Families Actually Face

Final expense insurance is whole life insurance with a smaller benefit. Your family can use the money however they need to.

⚱️

Funeral, Burial or Cremation

The service, the plot or urn, the headstone, and the fees that come with them.

🧾

Final Bills

Medical bills, credit cards or other debts that would otherwise fall to your family.

🏡

Room to Breathe

Travel for family, time off work, or simply a cushion while everything is settled.

Your Options

Two Ways to Qualify

Most people qualify one of two ways. We will tell you plainly which fits your health and budget.

📝

Simplified Issue

A short set of health questions and no medical exam. If you qualify, coverage can start right away.

🤝

Guaranteed-Issue Plans

Some plans ask no health questions at all. These plans usually pay the full benefit only after a waiting period, commonly two years, so we look at simplified-issue options first.

🔒

Coverage That Lasts

Final expense is a form of whole life insurance: as long as premiums are paid, it does not expire at a certain age.

Who It Helps

Is Final Expense Right for You?

It is often a fit if you are roughly 50 to 85, live on a fixed income, or have health conditions that make larger policies hard to get. If you need more coverage, for a mortgage or young children, we will show you term or whole life options too, and help Fort Sill families compare with VGLI.

Common Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does final expense insurance cost?

It depends on your age, health, tobacco use and the coverage amount. We quote options from several highly rated carriers so you can choose a monthly premium that fits your budget. The quote is free.

Can I get coverage with health problems?

Often, yes. Many simplified-issue plans accept common conditions such as controlled diabetes or high blood pressure. If not, guaranteed-issue plans ask no health questions, though they usually have a waiting period before the full benefit is paid.

Is there a waiting period?

Simplified-issue plans usually have none if you qualify. Guaranteed-issue plans usually do, commonly two years, and during that time they typically return premiums plus interest instead of the full benefit for death from illness.

What is the difference between burial insurance and life insurance?

Burial or final expense insurance is life insurance. It is whole life with a smaller benefit, sold with a simpler application. The benefit is paid to your beneficiary, who can use it for any cost.

Do you serve towns outside Lawton?

Yes. We help families across Comanche County and the surrounding area, including Cache, Elgin, Duncan, Anadarko and Frederick. We are licensed in Oklahoma and Missouri, so we cannot quote people who live in Texas.
